newsitem.title: GERMANY: Linotype says expects 1996 operating loss.
newsitem.headline: Linotype says expects 1996 operating loss.

text.p: German printing group Linotype-Hell AG said on Tuesday it expected to report a 1996 operating loss of about 73 million marks at the parent company level and about 82 million marks for the group.
Linotype said the forecasts did not include costs for restructuring measures.
The group said in December that it expected to make a loss of about 70 million marks in 1996 and would cut 1,200 jobs in a major restructuring to be completed in end-1997.
The revamping calls for Linotype to focus on its core business and centralise activities at its Kiel production site.
Linotype was taken over by printing machinery group Heidelberger Druckmaschinen AG earlier this year. Heidelberger Druck is in turn a subsidiary of Rheinelektra AG.
